findings.violating_statement: The identification section does not provide any information on the conformity assessment procedures, notified‑body resources or audit programme required by Annex VII 4 (a‑e).
findings.source_quote: The scope of this clinical evaluation includes the Double J Stent (Short Term), designed and manufactured by Biorad under the brand name DJS as mentioned below.
findings.explanation: Annex VII 4 (a) requires the notified body to assess documentation, define audit programmes, allocate responsibilities and qualified personnel. The CER section only lists the device name and variants and omits any reference to these conformity‑assessment requirements, indicating non‑compliance.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a paragraph stating that the conformity assessment procedures applicable to the Double J Stent (Short Term) have been identified, the notified body’s ability to assess the application has been confirmed, and that sufficient resources and an audit programme in line with Annex VII 4 (a‑e) are in place.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide the detailed information on absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, local tolerance and toxicity required by Annex II 6.c#1 for devices that are introduced into the human body.
findings.source_quote: Table 4: Regulatory details Basic UDI-DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit Blue (Short Term); 890551639TL. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue HC; 8905516101AW. ...
findings.explanation: Annex II 6.c#1 mandates inclusion of study protocols and data summaries for such devices. The administrative section only lists identifiers and certificates and contains no such clinical or pre‑clinical data, constituting a breach.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a dedicated subsection that includes the complete test protocols, methods of data analysis, and summaries of results for absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, local tolerance and toxicity studies as required.

findings.violating_statement: The report lacks any justification concerning the presence of CMR or endocrine‑disrupting substances as required by Annex II 6.d#1.
findings.source_quote: Table 4: Regulatory details Basic UDI-DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit Blue (Short Term); 890551639TL. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue HC; 8905516101AW. ...
findings.explanation: Annex II 6.d#1 requires a justification for CMR or endocrine‑disrupting substances. No such justification is present in the administrative particulars.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a justification statement, referencing the relevant sections of Annex I, that explains why the device does or does not contain CMR or endocrine‑disrupting substances.

findings.violating_statement: No description of the environmental conditions, sterilisation methods, validation reports or bioburden/pyrogen testing required by Annex II 6.e is provided.
findings.source_quote: Table 4: Regulatory details Basic UDI‑DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit Blue (Short Term); 890551639TL. ...
findings.explanation: Annex II 6.e mandates detailed information on manufacturing environment and sterilisation validation for sterile devices. The section only lists regulatory identifiers and does not address these requirements.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a subsection describing the manufacturing environmental conditions, sterilisation methods, and attach validation reports covering bioburden, pyrogen and sterilant residue testing.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not contain a description of methods used to ensure measurement accuracy as required by Annex II 6.f.
findings.source_quote: Table 4: Regulatory details Basic UDI‑DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit Blue (Short Term); 890551639TL. ...
findings.explanation: Annex II 6.f applies to devices with a measuring function. No information on measurement accuracy methods is present, indicating non‑compliance if the device has such a function.
findings.suggested_correction: If the device includes a measuring function, provide a description of the accuracy verification methods and results; otherwise, state that the device does not have a measuring function.

findings.violating_statement: Manufacturer name, registered trade name or trademark and business address are not provided in the device description
findings.source_quote: Double J Stent is used for treatment of the upper urinary tract are implantable devices that support the flow of the urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(c) requires the name, registered trade name or trademark of the manufacturer and the address of its registered place of business, which are absent from the description.
findings.suggested_correction: Include the manufacturer's name, registered trade name or trademark and the full address of its registered place of business in the device description.

findings.violating_statement: Information about an authorised representative is missing, which is required if the manufacturer is located outside the EU
findings.source_quote: Double J Stent is used for treatment of the upper urinary tract are implantable devices that support the flow of the urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(d) mandates that when the manufacturer’s registered place of business is outside the Union, the name and address of the authorised representative must be provided; the current text does not contain this information.
findings.suggested_correction: Add the name and address of the authorised representative when the manufacturer is based outside the EU.

findings.violating_statement: The CER section does not provide the device identification details, manufacturer name and address, or authorised representative information required by Annex I.23.b, Annex I.23.c and Annex I.23.d.
findings.source_quote: The Double J Stent (Short Term) is classified as a Class IIa medical device under Regulation (EU) 2017/745.
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.b requires details necessary for a user to identify the device, its packaging contents and intended purpose, which are not presented in the section. Annex I.23.c requires the name and address of the manufacturer, and Annex I.23.d requires the authorised representative details when the manufacturer is outside the Union. These mandatory labeling elements are absent, constituting a documentation non‑compliance.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a statement such as: "Device name: Double J Stent (Short Term); Model/Version: ...; Intended purpose: ...; Manufacturer: XYZ Ltd., 123 Street, City, Country; If applicable, Authorised Representative: ABC Ltd., 456 Avenue, EU Country."

findings.violating_statement: The technical specifications do not provide any information on conformity assessment required before placing the device on the market, which is mandatory under MDR Article 52.1.
findings.source_quote: MRI Compatibility; Specifications: Not specified in Technical File (no MR safety claim declared).
findings.explanation: Article 52.1 requires manufacturers to undertake an assessment of conformity of the device prior to market placement. The CER section lacks any statement or evidence that such an assessment has been performed, and even notes that MRI safety information is not specified, indicating incomplete conformity documentation.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a statement confirming that a conformity assessment has been completed in accordance with Annex IX–XI, and provide the relevant MRI safety classification and supporting test results.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide a clear specification of the device's intended purpose including indications, contra‑indications, patient target group and intended users as required.
findings.source_quote: Devices that support the flow of the urine from the kidneys to the bladder. These are made available with tapered ends to allow for ease of introduction over a compatible guidewire.
findings.explanation: Annex I 23.b requires a clear specification of the intended purpose, indications, contra‑indications, patient groups and intended users. The excerpt only describes a generic function and lacks explicit statements of indications, contra‑indications, target patient population and user categories, thus non‑compliant.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a dedicated section stating: "Intended purpose: to provide temporary urinary drainage in adult patients with ureteral obstruction. Indications: ... Contra‑indications: ... Target patient group: adults requiring short‑term stenting (60 min to 30 days). Intended users: urologists and trained healthcare professionals. "

findings.violating_statement: The description of accessories does not give healthcare professionals sufficient information to verify suitability or to select the appropriate accessories and software.
findings.source_quote: Umbilical cord clamp use to clamp or hold the pusher and Double J Stents or ureteral stents during insertion of stents over a guidewire (all category).
findings.explanation: Annex I 23.f requires information enabling the healthcare professional to verify if the device is suitable and to select corresponding software and accessories. The current text merely describes the function of the clamp without specifying compatibility criteria, sizing, or selection guidance, thus violating the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Include detailed selection criteria, e.g., "The umbilical cord clamp is compatible with pusher sizes 5‑10 Fr, intended for use with Double J Stents of length 24‑30 cm. No software integration is required."

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide the required specification of clinical benefits expected from the device as required by Annex I 23.c
findings.source_quote: The Double J Stent (Short Term) is a passive, implantable ureteral stent intended to support urine flow from the kidney to the bladder in cases of ureteral obstruction or impaired drainage.
findings.explanation: Annex I 23.c mandates a description of the clinical benefits to be expected where applicable. The section only describes the mechanism of action and intended use, but omits any statement of the clinical benefit such as improved drainage outcomes or reduced complications.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as: "The clinical benefit of the Double J Stent is to provide immediate restoration of urinary drainage, reducing pain and risk of renal damage associated with ureteral obstruction, and to facilitate patient recovery until definitive treatment can be performed."

findings.violating_statement: The report lacks a complete intended purpose specification, including contra‑indications, patient target group and intended users, as required by Annex I 23.b
findings.source_quote: The Double J Stent (Short Term) is a passive, implantable ureteral stent intended to support urine flow from the kidney to the bladder in cases of ureteral obstruction or impaired drainage.
findings.explanation: Annex I 23.b requires the device's intended purpose to be clearly specified with indications, contra‑indications, patient target groups and intended users. The section only states the general intended purpose and indications, but does not list contra‑indications, the specific patient population (e.g., adult patients with obstructive uropathy) or the intended users (e.g., urologists, interventional radiologists).
findings.suggested_correction: Expand the intended purpose description to include: "Contra‑indications: known allergy to device material, active urinary infection, non‑obstructive hydronephrosis. Target patient group: adult patients requiring temporary urinary drainage. Intended users: qualified urologists or interventional radiologists trained in ureteral stent placement."

findings.violating_statement: The CER section does not provide any information about labeling or instructions for use required by the MDR.
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device which is used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder in medical conditions like improper urine drainage, calculi in ureter, hydronephrosis, oxalate calculi, pyeloplasty with UPJ Obstruction, residual renal calculus, ureteral stricture.
findings.explanation: Annex I 23.1 requires that each device be accompanied by information needed to identify the device and its manufacturer, and any safety and performance information relevant to the user. The CER excerpt provides only a description of intended use and does not include any labeling or instructions for use, thus failing to meet this requirement.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a section detailing the label content and instructions for use, specifying device identification, manufacturer details, safety information, and performance data as required by Annex I 23.1.

findings.violating_statement: The intended purpose is not fully specified; indications, contraindications, patient target group and intended users are missing.
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(b) requires a clear specification of indications, contraindications, patient target group and intended users, which are not provided in the excerpt.
findings.suggested_correction: The device is intended for single‑use sterile internal drainage from the kidney to the bladder in adult patients with obstructive uropathy, contraindicated in patients with active urinary tract infection, and intended to be used by trained urologists or interventional radiologists.

findings.violating_statement: No clinical benefits are described, which are required when applicable.
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(c) mandates a specification of the clinical benefits to be expected; the section provides no such information.
findings.suggested_correction: The device is expected to provide rapid relief of urinary obstruction, reduce the risk of renal damage, and improve patient quality of life by restoring normal urine flow.

findings.violating_statement: The intended purpose of the device is not clearly stated as required for user identification and labeling
findings.source_quote: Double J Stent (Short term) is manufactured to meet requirements of medical conditions like Improper urine drainage, calculi in ureter, hydronephrosis, oxalate calculi, pyeloplasty with UPJ Obstruction, residual renal calculus, ureteral stricture.
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(b) requires the intended purpose of the device to be clearly communicated to the user. The CER section only lists medical conditions and does not explicitly state the device's intended purpose, which is a regulatory documentation gap.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a clear statement of the intended purpose, e.g., "The Double J Stent (Short term) is intended for temporary drainage of urine in patients with ureteral obstruction or postoperative ureteral healing."

findings.violating_statement: The identification section does not specify the intended purpose, target groups, clinical benefits or outcome parameters required by the clinical evaluation plan.
findings.source_quote: The scope of this clinical evaluation includes the Double J Stent (Short Term), designed and manufactured by Biorad under the brand name DJS as mentioned below.
findings.explanation: Annex XIV Part A paragraph (1)(a) requires the clinical evaluation plan to include a clear specification of the intended purpose, intended target groups, and a detailed description of intended clinical benefits with outcome parameters. The provided section only lists the device name and manufacturer, omitting these mandatory elements.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a detailed description of the device's intended purpose (e.g., urinary drainage), the specific patient population (e.g., adults requiring short‑term ureteral stenting), and the clinical benefits and outcome measures (e.g., relief of obstruction, incidence of migration, infection rates).

findings.violating_statement: No demonstration of equivalence to a similar device is provided, contrary to the requirement to evaluate clinical data relating to equivalent or similar devices.
findings.source_quote: The scope of this clinical evaluation includes the Double J Stent (Short Term), designed and manufactured by Biorad under the brand name DJS as mentioned below.
findings.explanation: Annex XIV Part A paragraph (3) mandates that, when a clinical evaluation is based on data from equivalent devices, the manufacturer must demonstrate technical, biological and clinical similarity. The section merely identifies the device without any equivalence justification or reference to comparable devices.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a justification of equivalence, comparing the Double J Stent (Short Term) to a previously marketed device with respect to design, materials, intended use, and clinical performance, and cite the supporting data.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not demonstrate that the Basic UDI‑DI was assigned before the manufacturer applied to the notified body, nor that the notified body’s certificate includes a reference to the Basic UDI‑DI as required by Art.29.3.
findings.source_quote: Basic UDI-DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit Blue (Short Term); 890551639TL. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue HC; 8905516101AW. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue Set; 890551640T5.
findings.explanation: Art.29.3 mandates that the Basic UDI‑DI be assigned before the manufacturer applies for the conformity assessment and that the notified body’s certificate reference this Basic UDI‑DI. The CER section only lists the Basic UDI‑DI codes without any statement confirming the timing of assignment or inclusion on the certificate, indicating non‑compliance.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement confirming that the Basic UDI‑DI was assigned prior to the application to the notified body and that the notified body’s certificate references the Basic UDI‑DI, e.g., "The Basic UDI‑DI was assigned on [date] before the application to TÜV SÜD Product Service GmbH, and the issued certificate includes a reference to this Basic UDI‑DI as required by Art.29.3."

findings.violating_statement: The device description does not provide any information on warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken or limitations of use for the Double J Stent.
findings.source_quote: Double J Stent is used for treatment of the upper urinary tract are implantable devices that support the flow of the urine from the kidneys to the bladder. Double J Stents can be used short-term for up to 30 days, or long-term for several months depending on the cause and course of treatment.
findings.explanation: Annex I, clause 23(s) requires that the device description include information that allows the user and/or patient to be informed of any warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken and limitations of use. The provided description contains only functional and usage details and omits all required safety information, constituting a breach of this clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a section detailing all relevant warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken in case of malfunction, and any limitations of use for the Double J Stent, in line with Annex I 23(s).

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide a confirmation that the device meets any defined chemical and/or physical specifications as required by Annex I 10.h.
findings.source_quote: The materials selected for device construction are widely used in urological medical devices and are suitable for short-term internal use.
findings.explanation: Annex I 10.h requires the manufacturer to confirm that the device meets defined chemical and physical specifications. The CER only states that the materials are widely used and suitable, without an explicit confirmation of compliance with the required specifications.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as: "All materials and components have been verified to meet the defined chemical and physical specifications outlined in the device's technical documentation, in accordance with Annex I 10.h of the MDR."

findings.violating_statement: The report does not include the required information on whether the single‑use device is reprocessed, as required by Annex VI A.2 point 2.6.
findings.source_quote: Single-use; Invasive via natural orifice;
findings.explanation: Annex VI A.2 requires the device information to state the reprocessed single‑use status (yes/no). The CER mentions the device is single‑use but does not explicitly state that it is not reprocessed.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a clear statement: "Reprocessed single‑use device: No" in the device information section.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide the user‑or‑patient information on warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken or limitations of use required by the MDR.
findings.source_quote: These are made available with tapered ends to allow for ease of introduction over a compatible guidewire. Further its smooth surface also provides for lesser trauma for the patients.
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.s#1 requires that the clinical evaluation report include information that allows the user and/or patient to be informed of any warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken and limitations of use. The CER section only describes the device’s physical characteristics and intended use, but omits any such safety information.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a subsection that lists all relevant warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken and usage limitations for the Double J Stent and its accessories, e.g., risk of migration, infection control measures, contraindications in patients with urinary tract obstruction, and handling instructions.

findings.violating_statement: The Clinical Evaluation Report does not provide the user/patient information on warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken or limitations of use required by Annex I.23.s
findings.source_quote: The mechanism of action is mechanical and is based on the following: 1. Internal Urinary Drainage The stent is placed within the ureter, extending from the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder. Its hollow tubular structure provides a conduit that allows urine to pass from the kidney to the bladder when normal ureteral flow is compromised.
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.s mandates that the device information include warnings, precautions, contraindications and limitations of use. The CER section only describes the mechanical principle of operation and does not contain any such safety information, representing a breach of the MDR requirement.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a subsection to the CER that details all relevant warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken in case of malfunction, environmental influences, and any limitations of use for the Double J Stent, referencing clinical data and risk analysis.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not specify the sterilisation method for the single‑use sterile device as required.
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device which is used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder in medical conditions like improper urine drainage, calculi in ureter, hydronephrosis, oxalate calculi, pyeloplasty with UPJ Obstruction, residual renal calculus, ureteral stricture.
findings.explanation: Clause [Annex.I.23.l] mandates that when a device is supplied sterile, the intended use section must include an indication of its sterile state and the sterilisation method. The CER only states the device is sterile but omits any description of the sterilisation method, breaching the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a statement such as: "The device is supplied sterile, using ethylene oxide sterilisation (ISO 11135) with validated parameters ensuring sterility assurance level of 10⁻⁶."

findings.violating_statement: Missing indication of the device's sterile state and the sterilisation method
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(l) requires that if the device is supplied sterile, the label must indicate its sterile state and the sterilisation method, which is not provided in the CER section.
findings.suggested_correction: Indicate that the device is supplied sterile and specify the sterilisation method (e.g., ethylene oxide, gamma irradiation).

findings.violating_statement: Missing declaration that the device is in a sterile condition
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(b) #2 requires a declaration that the device is in a sterile condition, which is absent from the provided text.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as "The device is supplied in a sterile condition."

findings.violating_statement: Missing instructions for damaged or unintentionally opened sterile packaging
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Annex I 23(l)#1 mandates that instructions be provided for the event of sterile packaging being damaged or opened before use; the CER does not contain such instructions.
findings.suggested_correction: Include instructions like "If the sterile packaging is damaged or opened, do not use the device and contact the manufacturer."

findings.violating_statement: The intended patient population description does not provide the required information on warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken and limitations of use for the device.
findings.source_quote: These medical conditions commonly occur in adult Male, Female during urological procedures.
findings.explanation: Annex I, clause 23(s) requires that the clinical evaluation report include information that allows the user/patient to be informed of any warnings, precautions, contraindications, measures to be taken and limitations of use. The CER section only lists medical conditions and demographic groups and omits any such safety information, thus breaching the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a subsection that details all relevant warnings, precautions, contraindications, required measures and limitations of use for the Double J Stent (Short term), e.g., "The device must not be used in patients with known hypersensitivity to the stent material, in cases of active urinary infection, or where there is a risk of migration. Users must monitor for signs of obstruction, infection, or haematuria and follow the recommended removal schedule within the specified short‑term period."

findings.violating_statement: The report mentions similar generic devices but does not provide the required technical, biological and clinical comparison to demonstrate equivalence as required by Annex XIV.A.3.
findings.source_quote: However, similar generic devices have been on the market for some time and have well-established technology (WET)
findings.explanation: Annex XIV.A.3 mandates a detailed justification of equivalence covering technical, biological and clinical characteristics. The CER only states that similar devices exist without the required comparative analysis, thus the equivalence claim is unsupported.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a detailed comparison of the Double J Stent/Kit with the referenced generic devices, addressing design, materials, intended use, clinical condition, patient population, and performance data to demonstrate no clinically significant differences.

findings.violating_statement: The clinical background does not provide a critical evaluation of the scientific literature that demonstrates equivalence of the device to the referenced devices or that the data adequately demonstrate compliance with the relevant general safety and performance requirements, as required by Art.61.3.a.
findings.source_quote: The included scientific articles collectively describe the medical condition addressed by the device, outlining its pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and epidemiological relevance. ... Evidence from the included publications also defines the typical target patient population, relevant comorbidities, and expected clinical outcomes associated with standard care.
findings.explanation: Art.61.3.a mandates a critical evaluation of the relevant scientific literature, including demonstration that the device under evaluation is equivalent to the devices described in the literature and that the data demonstrate compliance with safety and performance requirements. The provided section only describes the condition and existing practices without such critical assessment or equivalence justification, thus breaching the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a dedicated subsection that critically appraises the identified literature, explicitly demonstrating that the evaluated ureteral stent is equivalent to the devices discussed (e.g., "Double J" stents) in terms of design, materials, and intended use, and that the literature data confirm compliance with the applicable general safety and performance requirements.

findings.violating_statement: The report presents a comparison with alternative treatments but does not demonstrate equivalence of the Double J Stent to any other device as required by Annex XIV A.3.
findings.source_quote: The following table provides a comparison of the Double J Stent (Short Term) with alternative treatment options available for the management of ureteral obstruction and impaired urinary drainage.
findings.explanation: Annex XIV A.3 mandates that any clinical evaluation based on data from equivalent devices must include a justified demonstration of technical, biological and clinical equivalence. The section merely lists alternative options without any equivalence justification, violating this requirement.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a subsection that explicitly demonstrates equivalence, addressing technical, biological and clinical characteristics as specified in Annex XIV A.3, and provide scientific justification for using data from the listed alternatives.

findings.violating_statement: The section does not provide the comprehensive user/patient information on warnings, precautions, and limitations of use required by Annex I.23.s#1.
findings.source_quote: Risks / Limitations: Stent-related symptoms, hematuria, risk of infection, migration or encrustation if used beyond intended duration; requires removal.
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.s#1 requires that the device documentation contain detailed information enabling users and patients to be informed of all relevant warnings, precautions, contraindications and limitations. The CER only lists some risks without the full required information, thus not meeting the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Expand the risk/limitations description to include all required warnings, precautions, contraindications, and measures to be taken, ensuring the information aligns with the format stipulated in Annex I.23.s#1.

findings.violating_statement: The report asserts that no clinical investigation was performed based solely on MDR article 61, without demonstrating that an exemption under Art.61.4 applies
findings.source_quote: Hence, according to MDR article 61, no clinical investigation was performed.
findings.explanation: Art.61.4 requires clinical investigations for implantable devices unless the device is a modified version of a marketed device that meets the specific equivalence and notified‑body endorsement conditions. The CER provides no evidence of such an exemption, making the statement non‑compliant.
findings.suggested_correction: Provide justification that the device meets one of the exemptions listed in Art.61.4 (e.g., it is a modification of a marketed device with demonstrated equivalence endorsed by the notified body) or conduct and document a clinical investigation as required.

findings.violating_statement: The report relies on adverse event data of generic devices and does not describe a device‑specific post‑market clinical follow‑up (PMCF) plan as required for implantable/class III devices.
findings.source_quote: Adverse event data of generic devices
findings.explanation: Art.61.4 requires that for implantable or class III devices a PMCF plan be established and reviewed by the notified body. Using generic device data does not satisfy the requirement for device‑specific clinical evidence post‑market.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a detailed, device‑specific PMCF plan describing how post‑market data (including adverse events, complaints, and clinical follow‑up) will be collected, analysed and reported, and ensure it is endorsed by the notified body.

findings.violating_statement: The CER does not specify the intended purpose of the Double J Stent (Short Term) as required for the clinical evaluation plan.
findings.source_quote: The scope of this clinical evaluation includes the Double J Stent (Short Term), designed and manufactured by Biorad under the brand name DJS as mentioned below.
findings.explanation: Annex XIV Part A (1)(a) mandates that the clinical evaluation plan must include a clear specification of the intended purpose of the device, which is absent from the provided section.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as: "Intended purpose: The Double J Stent (Short Term) is intended for temporary ureteral drainage following urological procedures."

findings.violating_statement: The CER lacks identification of the target patient groups, indications and contraindications for the device.
findings.source_quote: The scope of this clinical evaluation includes the Double J Stent (Short Term), designed and manufactured by Biorad under the brand name DJS as mentioned below.
findings.explanation: Annex XIV Part A (1)(a) requires a clear specification of intended target groups with clear indications and contra‑indications, which is not provided in the section.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a target‑group description, e.g., "Target groups: adult patients requiring short‑term ureteral stenting; Indications: relief of ureteral obstruction; Contra‑indications: active urinary tract infection, known hypersensitivity to device materials."

findings.violating_statement: The CER does not describe the clinical benefits to patients or the outcome parameters to be measured.
